sentence: I have ______ cat. It's very friendly.
explanation: Use <a> before singular countable nouns starting with a consonant sound.

sentence: She is ______ honest person.
explanation: Use <an> before words that start with a silent 'h' (vowel sound): <an honest>.

sentence: I saw ______ elephant at the zoo yesterday.
explanation: Use <an> before words starting with a vowel sound: <an elephant>.

sentence: Can you close ______ door, please?
explanation: Use <the> when both speaker and listener know which specific thing is meant.

sentence: ______ sun rises in the east.
explanation: Use <the> with unique things — there is only one sun.

sentence: I want to be ______ engineer when I grow up.
explanation: Use <an> before vowel sounds. 'Engineer' starts with /ɛ/.

sentence: She goes to ______ school every morning.
explanation: No article with 'go to school' when referring to the regular activity (not the building).

sentence: He plays ______ guitar very well.
explanation: Use <the> with musical instruments: <play the guitar>, <play the piano>.

sentence: I had ______ breakfast at 7 o'clock.
explanation: No article with meal names: <have breakfast>, <have lunch>, <have dinner>.

sentence: There is ______ university near my house.
explanation: Use <a> before 'university' because it starts with /juː/ (consonant sound), not a vowel sound.

sentence: ______ water is important for life.
explanation: No article with uncountable nouns when speaking in general.

sentence: She bought ______ new dress. ______ dress was blue.
explanation: Use <a> for first mention (new information), <the> for second mention (already known).
tip: Two gaps: first mention vs. second mention

sentence: I like ______ dogs. They are loyal animals.
explanation: No article when talking about things in general (all dogs, not specific ones).

sentence: He goes to ______ bed at 10 pm every night.
explanation: No article with 'go to bed' when talking about the activity of sleeping.

sentence: She plays ______ tennis on Saturdays.
explanation: No article with sports: <play tennis>, <play football>, <play basketball>.

sentence: Look! ______ moon is beautiful tonight.
explanation: Use <the> with unique objects — there is only one moon.

sentence: I need ______ umbrella. It's raining.
explanation: Use <an> before words starting with a vowel sound: <an umbrella>.

sentence: He is ______ best student in the class.
explanation: Use <the> with superlatives: <the best>, <the tallest>, <the most interesting>.

sentence: We live in ______ small apartment in the city center.
explanation: Use <a> when mentioning something for the first time (non-specific).

sentence: I always have ______ coffee in the morning.
explanation: No article with uncountable nouns in general statements about habits.
